name: Enrolled students
definition: Students enrolled at the school on the October 1 count, by grade and student group
aggregation: sum across schools; never sum grade ALL with grade rows
breaks: Coverage break between 2013-14 and 2014-15: files for 2009-10 to 2013-14 cover district schools only (131,894 students in 2013-14); from 2014-15 they include charter and alternative schools (197,694). Do not draw a trend line across that break without labeling it. 2014-15 to 2018-19 files were reposted in Aug 2025 under new suppression rules. 2010-11 Black, Hispanic, American Indian, and multiracial counts are withheld (zeros in the source; corrections/enrollment.csv).
usage_notes: Groups under the district's threshold are suppressed (2009-10 to 2013-14: whole rows with 20 or fewer students). Economically disadvantaged counts exist only for 2012-13 and 2013-14 and use a different method from the later CEP rate. The October 1 count is the state funding count. In October 2026 the Inquirer reported the district re-enrolled about 720 students just before the deadline and acknowledged about 2,000 improper withdrawals, so a count can be affected by how withdrawals are processed; read the 2026-27 count with that in mind and do not compare it directly with earlier years until the district explains.

name: Economically disadvantaged rate (CEP)
definition: Share of students the district counts as economically disadvantaged under the federal Community Eligibility Provision method
breaks: CEP direct-certification method; not comparable to free/reduced lunch counts from other places
usage_notes: A poverty proxy. Do not use alone to rank or label schools.

name: Students by catchment and school
definition: Students who live in a catchment (by last address on file at the Oct 1 snapshot) and are enrolled at a given school
usage_notes: Catchment 'not available' means the address could not be placed; destinations outside the district list are placeholder schools (cyber and out-of-city charters).

name: Building capacity
definition: Seats the district counts for the school's building
aggregation: sum per building, not per school (co-located schools share a building)
breaks: Facilities planning capacity figures have shifted between releases
usage_notes: Check co-location before comparing; see facilities data gaps.

name: Total enrollment (retention file)
definition: Total students enrolled at the school as reported in the district's catchment retention file
usage_notes: May differ slightly from enrollment_count totals because of snapshot and program rules.

name: Catchment size
definition: Students living in the school's catchment who are enrolled in any public school (district, charter, or cyber)
aggregation: not aggregable across levels (ES, MS, HS catchments overlap)
breaks: Catchment boundaries change by year
usage_notes: Only neighborhood (catchment) schools have catchments.

name: Catchment students attending
definition: Students who live in the school's catchment and attend the school
usage_notes: Numerator of both retention percentages.

name: Enrollment to catchment ratio
definition: School enrollment divided by catchment size
usage_notes: High values can mean a small catchment or many students from elsewhere.

name: Share of catchment students who attend
definition: Catchment students attending the school as a percent of all students living in the catchment
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
usage_notes: Denominator is residents, not enrollment. Citywide (sum of attending over sum of catchment size, this project's calculation): 47.4% in 2016-17, 38.1% to 38.8% from 2021-22 to 2025-26.

name: Share of enrollment from the catchment
definition: Catchment students attending the school as a percent of the school's enrollment
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average
usage_notes: Denominator is the school's enrollment, not catchment residents.

name: Public school students living in the neighborhood (estimate)
definition: Students living in catchments, spread over neighborhoods by where each catchment's 2020 population lives (catchment_flow_to_neighborhood_v1)
aggregation: sum across neighborhoods (not exactly additive to citywide because of unplaced students)
breaks: 2016-17 and 2017-18 have many more students with unplaced addresses (15,735 and 27,911 vs about 2,000 recently), so early estimates undercount
usage_notes: Estimate, not a count. Under 20 is suppressed.

name: Neighborhood students attending their catchment school (estimate)
definition: Of resident students, those enrolled at the school whose catchment they live in (catchment_flow_to_neighborhood_v1)
breaks: 2016-17 and 2017-18 have many more students with unplaced addresses (15,735 and 27,911 vs about 2,000 recently), so early estimates undercount
usage_notes: Estimate. Under 20 is suppressed.

name: Share of neighborhood students attending their catchment school (estimate)
definition: attending_catchment_school_est divided by resident_students_est
breaks: 2016-17 and 2017-18 have many more students with unplaced addresses (15,735 and 27,911 vs about 2,000 recently), so early estimates undercount
usage_notes: Suppressed when the numerator is under 20. Describes family choices and seat availability together; not a measure of school quality.

name: Percent at a performance level (district PSSA/Keystone)
definition: Share of tested students at each performance level; stored 0 to 100 (older files used fractions and were rescaled)
aggregation: recompute from counts; do not average

No 2019-20 or 2020-21 district files. Keystone exams replaced grade 11 PSSA from 2012-13.
usage_notes: Matches Future Ready ELA proficiency at r = 0.996 (2018-19) for schools in both. Read with poverty and growth; never rank on it.

name: Enrollment (state Fast Facts)
definition: Students enrolled at the school as reported by PDE in School Fast Facts
usage_notes: State count; may differ from the district's October 1 count (enrollment_count) because of snapshot date and program rules. Covers district and charter schools on one definition.

name: Share of enrollment by student group (state Fast Facts)
definition: Percent of the school's students in the group (student_group): economically disadvantaged, English learner, special education, gifted, homeless, foster care, military-connected, female, male, or a race/ethnicity group
breaks: Foster care is blank in 2024-25; gifted is reported as zero for many schools that may simply not report it.
usage_notes: Economically disadvantaged uses PDE's definition, not the district's CEP rate; do not mix the two in one trend.

name: Comparison with poverty peers
definition: A school's result next to the 15 non-selective schools in its grade band with the closest student poverty share: peer median, peer middle half (25th-75th percentile), difference from the peer median, and position (above, within, or below the peer range). Columns of derived/peer_comparison; method poverty_peers_k15_v1
breaks: Census bases switch ACS period between 2019-20 and 2020-21. Student-poverty basis has almost no 2017-18 district comparisons (the state file leaves the figure blank for district schools).
usage_notes: Facts, not rankings: never sort schools by it or combine it into a score. Three poverty bases side by side (school students' state econ disadvantaged share; ACS child poverty of the school's catchment; enrollment-weighted ACS child poverty where the school's students live). The basis changes the position for about half of schools, so show bases together. Positions repeat only moderately across non-overlapping periods (r 0.60 proficiency, 0.34-0.45 growth). Selective-admission schools are not compared. Census bases carry basis_moe and position_robust (same position at both edges of the poverty figure's margin). Robust: high schools 84-97%, K-8 47-64% (2018-2025); show a census-based position only where it is robust.

name: People in poverty (ACS)
definition: Share of people for whom poverty status is determined whose income is below the poverty level (B17001)
breaks: Two ACS periods: 2015-2019 (2010 tracts, crosswalked through 2020 blocks by 2020 population) and 2020-2024 (2020 tracts). Peer comparisons use 2015-2019 for school years through 2019-20 and 2020-2024 after. Income is in each period's own dollars (2019 or 2024): adjust for inflation before comparing.
usage_notes: Citywide 21.4% (2020-2024). Every value has a margin of error (moe, 90% level), numerator and denominator MOEs, a coefficient of variation (cv), and reliability (high under 15%, medium 15-30%, low over 30%). Rollup MOEs use Census approximation formulas and are approximate. Typical child-poverty MOE: tract +/-13 points, elementary catchment +/-9.5, high school catchment +/-4.8, neighborhood +/-8.6 (2020-2024).

name: Children in poverty (ACS)

name: Students expelled (CRDC)
definition: Students expelled with or without educational services (zero-tolerance expulsions are a subset and not added)
breaks: Collections every other year: 2011-12, 2013-14, 2015-16, 2017-18, 2020-21 (mostly virtual: near zero), 2021-22. 2011-12 disability and English learner counts look under-reported; 2013-14 and 2011-12 referrals to law enforcement are not comparable with later years (see docs/DISCIPLINE.md).

name: Painted components tested for lead (XRF)
definition: Painted surfaces (walls, door frames, sills, radiators, ...) tested with an XRF analyzer in the school's most recent full lead-safe assessment, summed over its buildings
breaks: Point-in-time: one assessment per building, done in different years (2017 to 2026). sy = school year the assessment ended.
usage_notes: Extracted from the district's lead-safe assessment PDFs (env results module). Schools sharing a building each get the building's figures. Buildings that are not schools (annexes, field houses, offices) are in school_lead_paint only.

name: Painted components with lead paint
definition: Components the inspector called positive for lead-based paint, in the most recent full assessment
breaks: Point-in-time; see lead_paint_components_tested.
usage_notes: The inspector's call as published. Firms cite different cutoffs; school_lead_paint also has the count at or above the federal 1.0 mg/cm2 level. Intact lead paint is managed in place; damaged lead paint is the hazard.

name: Lead-painted components with damaged paint
definition: Components positive for lead paint that also had damaged (flaking, peeling, chipping) paint at assessment, the hazard lead-safe certification requires fixing
breaks: Point-in-time; see lead_paint_components_tested.
usage_notes: Damage was recorded before stabilization; a later certification report may show it fixed. Square feet are in school_lead_paint.

name: Drinking water outlets tested for lead
definition: Water outlets (hydration stations, fountains, faucets, food-prep and ice-maker outlets) sampled in the school's most recent lead-in-water test, summed over its buildings
breaks: Point-in-time: the district retests each school every five years; most current letters are from 2025 and 2026. sy = school year of sampling.
usage_notes: Extracted from the district's water results letters. Schools sharing a building each get the building's figures. Results for each outlet are in school_water_lead.

name: Drinking water outlets above the lead action level
definition: Outlets whose first sample was above the district's 10 ppb action level in the most recent test (the outlet is shut off, then fixed and retested)
breaks: Point-in-time; see water_outlets_tested.
usage_notes: The district's action level (10 ppb) is stricter than the federal 15 ppb level for water systems. Follow-up letters (follow_up = true in school_water_lead) record the corrective action and retest result.

name: Asbestos-containing materials on record
definition: Entries in the building's room-by-room asbestos log that are confirmed or assumed to contain asbestos (one entry per material per space), from the most recent 6-month or 3-year AHERA report
breaks: Point-in-time: the most recent report, mostly 2025-26. sy = school year of the report.
usage_notes: Extracted from the district's AHERA reports. Managed in place, intact asbestos is legal and common in older buildings; the count reflects building age and size as much as risk. Amounts by unit (SF, LF, EA) are in building_asbestos. Annexes have their own building codes and are not added to the main school.

name: Asbestos-containing materials with damage
definition: Confirmed or assumed asbestos entries with a damaged amount above zero at the most recent inspection
breaks: Point-in-time; see asbestos_items.
usage_notes: Damage as the inspector recorded it; repairs after the inspection appear in the next report. Damaged amounts by unit are in building_asbestos.

name: Facility condition index (FCI)
definition: Cost of the site's assessed repair needs divided by its replacement value
breaks: 2020 assessment cycle by Parsons; reports dated 2021-22; 76 district sites (the reports the district posted). sy = school year of the report date.
usage_notes: District tiers: under 15% minimal; 15-25% refurbish systems; 25-45% replace systems; 45-60% consider major renovation; over 60% consider closing or replacement. Higher is worse. Site figures: a site's buildings and grounds together; schools sharing a site each get its figures. Detail by building in facility_condition_part and by system in facility_condition_system.

name: Facility condition score
definition: Parsons condition score for the site (100% minus FCI, as reported)
breaks: 2020 assessment cycle by Parsons; reports dated 2021-22; 76 district sites (the reports the district posted). sy = school year of the report date.
usage_notes: Higher is better. Site figures: a site's buildings and grounds together; schools sharing a site each get its figures. Detail by building in facility_condition_part and by system in facility_condition_system.

name: Educational suitability score
definition: How well the building suits its educational program (space, layout, specialized rooms), as Parsons scored it
breaks: 2020 assessment cycle by Parsons; reports dated 2021-22; 76 district sites (the reports the district posted). sy = school year of the report date.
usage_notes: Higher is better; missing for 8 sites. Site figures: a site's buildings and grounds together; schools sharing a site each get its figures. Detail by building in facility_condition_part and by system in facility_condition_system.

name: Overall school facility score
definition: Parsons combined score of condition and suitability
breaks: 2020 assessment cycle by Parsons; reports dated 2021-22; 76 district sites (the reports the district posted). sy = school year of the report date.
usage_notes: Higher is better; missing for 8 sites. Site figures: a site's buildings and grounds together; schools sharing a site each get its figures. Detail by building in facility_condition_part and by system in facility_condition_system.
